The Police Sub-Inspector of Hebbala Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

2. Prosecution Case: The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Shilpa Mary and the accused took place in the year 2008 and they were resided at No.175, 1 st Cross, V.Nagenahalli, within the limits of Hebbala Police Station, Bengaluru City, wherein the accused started ill-treating CW1 by suspecting her character, abused and beaten her, subjected her to mental and physical cruelty and thrown her out of the house.
3. First Information Report:

Upon the receipt of private complaint, CW8 Sri Andani., HC of Hebbala Police Station, registered Crime No.168/2020 against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers and drawn spot mahazar on 27-09-2020 as per Ex.P2.
4. Investigation: Thereafter CW9 Sri Rajesh.V.M., PSI, continued the investigation, recorded the statement of witnesses, secured the documents from CW1 as per Ex.P3 to Ex.P5 and submitted charge sheet against accused for the alleged offence.
5.
The accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 05-10-2021.

sentences.text: 6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court has taken cognizance for the offence alleged against the accused.
7. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 9 witnesses, examined 1 witness and exhibited 5 documents and closed their side.
During the cross examination of PW1, the counsel for accused has got marked one document as Ex.D1.

The learned Senior APP prays for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused have sort out the differences of opinion between them and residing together under one roof and hence the examination of CW2 to CW9 has been dispensed with by the order dated 17/12/2025.
10.

Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused was examined as per section 313 of Cr.P.C, wherein he denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witnesses and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.
2. What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1: In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution examined the witness which is as follows (i) CW1 by name Smt Shilpa Mary, being informant examined as PW1 deposed that on 30/09/2008 she got married with Accused, after marriage they were resided at Hebbal, where accused started ill-treating her by suspecting her, abused, assaulted her and forced to bring dowry and hence she Shilpameri vs Vinod Richard on 18 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31589406/
3 lodged complaint before police station as per Ex.P1, police conducted Ex.P2 mahazar.
Further, she identified her marriage certificate, marriage invitation card and Family photo as per Ex.P3 to Ex.P5 15.
Evidence of Prosecution must be established that the accused subjected the PW1 to mental and physical cruelty.

Mere omnibus statement regarding harassment does not ipso facto makes out a case under section 498A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the overt acts attributed by the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt and the said principle is appreciated in case of Sakharam and another vs State of Maharastra reported in (2003) 12 SCC 368.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Basing this decision, the present cases are taken up for discussion.
16. It is relevant to reiterate Section 498A of Indian Penal Code which reads as under Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty --

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

-- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

For commission of an offence under Section 498- A of IPC, the following necessary ingredients require to be satisfied:
(a) The woman must be married;
(b) She must be subjected to cruelty or harassment; and (c) Such cruelty or harassment must have been shown either by husband of the woman or by the relative of her husband and the said principle is appreciated in the case of U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757.
17.

entities.text: U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Every harassment does not amount to "cruelty" within the meaning of Section 498-A.

For the purpose of Section 498-A, harassment simpliciter is not "cruelty" and it is only when harassment is committed for the purpose of coercing a woman or any other person related to her to meet an unlawful demand for property, etc. that it amounts to "cruelty" punishable under Section 498-A IPC and the said principle is appreciated in the case of State of A.P. vs. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported Shilpameri vs Vinod Richard on 18 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31589406/
4 in (2008) 15 SCC 582.
18.

entities.text: State of A.P. vs. M. Madhusudhan Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Cruelty can either be mental or physical.
It is difficult for straitjacket the term cruelty by means of a definition because cruelty is a relative term.

What constitutes cruelty for one person may not constitute cruelty for another person and the said principle is appreciated in the case of G.V.
Siddaramesh v. State of Karnataka reported in (2010) 3 SCC 152.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The concept of cruelty and its effect varies from individual to individual, also depending upon the social and economic status to which such person belongs and the said principle is appreciated in the case of Gananath Pattnaik v.
State of Orissa reported in (2002) 2 SCC 619.
19.

sentences.text: No doubt, this court cannot expect any evidence for the matrimonial offences when it was taken place within the four walls however the allegation made by the PW1 has to be proved by adducing her cogent evidence.
Though the PW1 has initially supported the prosecution case, however subsequent to the evidence given, deposed in her cross examination as under

Thus, it appears from the cross examination of PW1 being material witness did not support the prosecution case for coherence with the contents of complaint and chief-in-examination on account of settlement between them and residing together under one roof.
20.

This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution case that would not helpful as PW1 herself did not support the prosecution case in the cross examination.

This court has dispensed with the examination of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature and hence taken the prosecution evidence as closed after examination of police official witnesses.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

sentences.text: By basing aforesaid principle by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the above case is applicable to this case as well.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 is answered in the negative.
21. Point No.2:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code (ii) Accused is set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C, his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
